questions.problem: Which of the following shaded areas describes the region bounded by the inequality $8x-4y<12?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we convert the inequality into slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}8x-4y & <12 \\ -4y & <-8x+12 \\ 4y & >8x-12 \\ y & >2x-3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we proceed as usual. We start by drawing the corresponding straight line $y=2x-3.$ Since the inequality involves a 'strictly greater than' sign, the line $y=2x-3$ itself is *not* part of the solution. Therefore, we draw a dashed line.

Then, we need to decide whether to shade above or below the line. The inequality $y>2x-3$ refers to the $y$-values that are *greater than* those on the line $y=2x-3,$ so we shade *above* the line.

canonical_examples.problem: Sketch the solutions to the inequality $x+2y < 4$ in the $xy$-plane.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we convert the inequality into slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2y & <4 \\ 2y & <-x+4 \\ y & <-\frac{1}{2}x+2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we proceed as usual. We start by drawing the corresponding straight line 

$$
y=-\dfrac{1}{2}x+2.
$$

Since the inequality involves a 'strictly less than' sign, the line $y=-\dfrac{1}{2}x+2$ itself is *not* part of the solution. Therefore, we draw a dashed line.

Then, we must decide whether to shade above or below the line. The inequality 

$$
y < -\dfrac{1}{2}x+2
$$

refers to the $y$-values that are *less than* those on the line $y = -\dfrac{1}{2}x+2,$ so we shade *below* the line.
